subject.title: Agent-scoped tools.allow may not restrict built-in tools in the provider-visible tool set

question: When an agent has a non-empty `tools.allow`, should any forced built-in tool remain provider-visible without being named by the allowlist?
rationale: The public documentation describes a non-empty allowlist as exclusive, but the report specifically asks whether any forced-tool exception is intentional; that security boundary must be explicit before a reproduction or repair is accepted as complete.

options.title: Make allowlists strictly exclusive
options.body: Treat every provider-visible built-in, plugin, and bundled tool as blocked unless it matches the resolved allowlist or a documented policy expansion.

options.title: Document narrow forced tools
options.body: Retain only specifically named forced tools, document the exception and threat model, and add tests proving those tools are the sole exception.

recommendation.title: Make allowlists strictly exclusive
recommendation.body: Treat every provider-visible built-in, plugin, and bundled tool as blocked unless it matches the resolved allowlist or a documented policy expansion.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged final-policy work is the closest established ownership signal for the complete effective-tool-list invariant.
